report.source_text: Her pathology showed that the left ovary displayed near-complete replacement by a diffuse proliferation of large somewhat pleomorphic cells (Figure 2), with prominent nucleoli (Figure 3), numerous mitotic figures, admixed body macrophages, and punctate areas of necrosis. The cells were negative for AE1/AE3, S100, CD30, and cyclin D1.

clinician.final_diagnosis: high-grade CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the left ovary
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old female presented with generalized fatigue, lower abdominal discomfort, and 40 pounds unintentional weight loss. Imaging revealed a left heterogeneous ovarian/adnexal mass and an enlarged left adrenal gland. Biopsy demonstrated diffuse proliferation of large pleomorphic malignant lymphoid cells expressing CD20, PAX5, MYC, with a high Ki-67 proliferation index (>90%) and absence of markers AE1/AE3, S100, CD30, and cyclin D1. FISH analysis revealed BCL6 and MYC rearrangements without BCL2 rearrangement. Immunohistochemical profile indicated non-GCB subtype DLBCL. Clinical follow-up showed remission 1.5 years post-treatment monitored by serial PET scans.
